name: Lydia Avery Coonley Ward
bio: Lydia Avery Coonley Ward (born 31 January 1845) was an American writer of devotional and reflective verse, who was living at Wyoming, New York, when The Home Book of Verse (1912) was compiled.
Her short poems "To-day" and "Heredity" were reprinted in that anthology.

poems.title: Heredity
poems.author: Lydia Avery Coonley Ward
poems.collection: The Home Book of Verse, ed. Burton Egbert Stevenson (1912)
poems.text:
Why bowest thou, O soul of mine,
Crushed by ancestral sin?
Thou hast a noble heritage,
That bids thee victory win.
The tainted past may bring forth flowers,
As blossomed Aaron’s rod;
No legacy of sin annuls
Heredity from God.

poems.title: To-day
poems.author: Lydia Avery Coonley Ward
poems.collection: The Home Book of Verse, ed. Burton Egbert Stevenson (1912)
poems.text:
Why fear to-morrow, timid heart?
Why tread the future’s way?
We only need to do our part
To-day, dear child, to-day.

The past is written! Close the book
On pages sad and gay;
Within the future do not look,
But live to-day—to-day.

’Tis this one hour that God has given;
His Now we must obey;
And it will make our earth his heaven
To live to-day—to-day.
